title: Lenticular Commitment Log — Diego Rinaldi
content:
Purpose:
A compact scratchpad oriented toward small, repeatable commitments (lenticular shifts) that compound into measurable weekly outcomes. Not a polished plan — working thinking, experiments, and a ledger for the next 8 weeks.

Context / heuristics I want to try:
- Make commitments that are clear, time-boxed (<= 90m), and repeatable for 3 consecutive days before expanding.
- Track both adherence (did the action happen) and signal (did it produce measurable progress toward KPI).
- Favor micro-A/B tests rather than large policy changes.

Current quarter (Q1 2026) personal OKR draft:
- O: Ship two small, production-ready observability helpers for my team and reduce mean time-to-insight for alerts.
  - KR1: 2 helpers merged + 1 rollout doc by 2026-03-31.
  - KR2: Reduce time-to-debug on top-10 alerts from 48h -> 24h (measured on retrospective samples).
  - KR3: Conduct 3 post-launch quick evals and capture 5 real user issues.

Weekly ledger (compact view — 6 week rolling):
Week | Micro-commitment | Planned time | Done | Signal (% improvement or note)
Wk1  (2026-02-02) | Draft helper A README + 2 unit tests | 60m | yes | sample fix for alert flow found
Wk2  (2026-02-09) | Prototype helper A CLI + demo | 90m | partial | CLI shows quicker stack trace extraction (+10% dev time)
Wk3  (2026-02-16) | Ship helper A PR -> review | 45m | yes | PR merged; 1 regression found by CI
Wk4  (2026-02-23) | Instrument alert path for helper A | 60m | no | blocked: need infra creds
Wk5  (2026-03-02) | Shadow rollout helper A -> 5% traffic | 30m | partial | telemetry noisy, need better labels
Wk6  (2026-03-09) | Retro + doc for helper A | 45m | yes | captured 3 user tweaks

Notes from ledger:
- 60–90m commitments feel doable; <30m commitments often deprioritized.
- Partial completions usually due to context-switching or blocked dependencies. Plan: convert blocked items into dependency cards and timebox follow-ups.

Experiment log (micro A/Bs):
- Experiment 1: Two-day block vs five 30m blocks for focused work on helper A. Result: two-day 90m block yielded deeper progress; fewer interruptions. Hypothesis holds for tasks requiring context rebuild.
- Experiment 2: Visible early demo (5min) to team on Tuesday vs solo finish then ship Friday. Result: early demo surfaced integration needs earlier; reduced rework.

Weekly metrics (simple signals I check weekly):
- Timeblocked hours completed: 6–9 hours (target 8).
- Micro-commitment completion rate (last 6 weeks): 67%
- Ticket churn (work reopened for helper A): 2 (target <=1)
- Mean time to first feedback on PRs: 14h (target <=12h)

Failure modes / mitigations:
- FM1: Over-specified commitments -> paralysis. Mitigation: split into a 2-step tiny deliverable and a follow-up ticket.
- FM2: Context switching during 90m blocks -> low depth. Mitigation: set Do Not Disturb, schedule on calendar, and prep a 5-line context note before block.
- FM3: Hidden infra blockers -> slows weekly cadence. Mitigation: proactively list dependencies at start of week and escalate by mid-week.

Quick retrospective (last 6 weeks):
- Wins: shipped a minimal helper that actually reduced a manual debugging step; learned that demos accelerate integration.
- Pain: telemetry labeling was an afterthought — plan to add a labeling checklist for next helper.

Next actions (prioritized):
1) Resolve infra creds blocker (create ticket + ping infra owner) — estimate 30m.
2) Add telemetry label checklist to helper template — 45m.
3) Run 2-day deep block on helper B prototype this coming Wed/Thu — reserve 3h each day.
4) Draft short onboarding notes and a one-slide demo for Eng Sync.

Open questions / deliberate unknowns:
- Is the 90m sweet spot generalizable to collaboration-heavy tasks? Need to run with pair sessions.
- How to reliably measure "time-to-insight" change for alerts without large sampling noise? Next step: pick 10 sample incidents and timestamp key milestones.

Sign-off / cadence:
- Weekly check-in on Mondays (10m) to set 3 micro-commitments, quick retro every 4 weeks.
- Update this ledger after each weekly retro.

Last quick log entry: 2026-03-10 09:12 — infra creds ticket created (IR-1123), scheduled demo for 2026-03-16.

Notes-to-self: Avoid making the commitments aspirational — keep them atomic and measurable. The lenticular metaphor: small tilted commitments that change the visible outcome when viewed from the right cadence.
